record.original_question: Given a prescribed number, divide it into two parts so that both parts are perfect cubes.

evidence.quote: Problem 27. Divide a given number into two cubic numbers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Decision problem: Given a positive rational number $N$, decide whether there exist rational numbers $x,y \in \mathbb{Q}$ such that
$$x^3 + y^3 = N,$$
and, when such a decomposition exists, exhibit one explicitly. Equivalently, characterize the set of rationals (in particular, positive integers) $N$ that can be written as the sum of two rational cubes, and provide an effective procedure that, on input $N$, determines whether $N$ lies in this set and produces a witness $(x,y) \in \mathbb{Q}^2$ if it does.
artifact.status_search_result: The general decision problem of determining whether a given integer is a sum of two rational cubes is a classical Diophantine problem that remains open. For |n|>2, n is a sum of two rational cubes iff a certain elliptic curve E_n has positive Mordell–Weil rank, which connects the problem to the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture. Substantial partial progress exists (Bhargava–Elkies–Shnidman density results, infinite families in arithmetic progressions, results for integers with few prime factors), but no general algorithm is known.

status_evidence.title: Integers that are the sum of two rational cubes (Bhargava slides)
status_evidence.snippet: Classical Diophantine problem: which integers are cube sums? Connected to ranks of elliptic curves E_n: x^3+y^3=n.
status_evidence.claim: The problem reduces to determining positivity of ranks of certain elliptic curves, an open question.

status_evidence.title: Integers expressible as the sum of two rational cubes
status_evidence.snippet: A positive proportion of integers are expressible as the sum of two rational cubes, and a positive proportion are not.
status_evidence.claim: Partial density results are known but no full characterization/algorithm.

status_evidence.title: Binary Cubic Forms and Rational Cube Sum Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on rational cube sum problem for restricted families of integers.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research, indicating problem is not fully resolved.
